newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa govt pension fund targetting cash, shares.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa govt pension fund targetting cash, shares.

text.p: South Africa's government pension fund, seeking to diversify its asset base, will not be rushing back into the bond market when it receives hefty coupon payments in August, an official said on Thursday.
Instead it would look to top up its cash reserves while continuing to broaden its exposure to equities, he told Reuters.

The Public Investment Commissioners (PIC), which manages government's 126 billion rand pension fund, currently has a 58 percent weighting in bonds, with about 27 percent in equities and the rest in cash and money market instruments.
In August, coupons of about eight billion rand on a variety of government stocks will be paid, mostly on bigger stocks like the R150 and R153.

According to the March Reserve Bank Quarterly Bulletin, the PIC holds 40 percent of the 17.11 billion rand outstanding on the 12 percent R150 and 26 percent of the 18.627 billion rand outstanding on the 13 percent R153.
Bond traders said they had been expecting the bulk of the coupon flows to the PIC to be rolled over back into existing bonds.
But the PIC official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said that its current intentions were to top up its cash reserves.
"We are not going to plough into the market with the cash and try and invest it straight away. We will just top up our cash reserves," he said.
"If we find there is a need for bonds we will do so, but at the moment we are not rushing after bonds at all."

This approach was part of a programme initiated in 1995 aimed at broadening its exposure to equities, he said, noting the PIC was "engineering" a shift of about two to three percent a year towards equities.
"We have been very careful over the last three years...we haven't invested much in the bond market. That will be the case in August," he said.

The coupon flows will come at the same time as the 8.8 billion rand redemption of the R119 stock, which has raised concerns among some analysts that the money markets will be swamped with liquidity in August.
But Eric Wood, head of Investec Trading, said the bond market was already seeing demand for both options and gilts ahead of the cash injection.
"Our feeling is that a lot of it is being sorted out right now. We are seeing a fair amount of gilt buying as well as a fair amount of options trade," Wood said.
"People are looking to buy at the money calls going into August and write out the money calls on the back of that on the expectation that they are going to receive a fair amount of cash," he said.

Mike Lamont, director of Standard Bank's fixed interest division, said that much of the R119 stock, currently a first tier asset, appeared to be held by commercial banks and would probably be directed towards Treasury Bills and short-term maturity bonds like the R147 and R148.

He noted that the Reserve Bank was unlikely to have much difficulty in meeting the cash requirement of the coupon payments and redemptions, having already pre-funded in the Treasury Bill market as well as offshore.

Roelf du Plooy, deputy general manager of the Reserve Bank's money and capital market division, said any excess liquidity that did surface in the markets in August was likely to be mopped up by the central bank.
"It is difficult to say what the liquidity situation will be in August, but if there an excess of liquidity the Bank will try to absorb some of it," du Plooy said.
